_comment: Routing table for bin/llm-router. Data, not code, so a tier can be added or re-ordered without touching the server. Order matters: demotion walks DOWN this list, and the last tier must always be one that works with no network and no subscription — it is the floor.

tiers.name: local-small
tiers.note: Mechanical work only: a rename, a one-line fix, a reformat. Chosen by jev's judge_model_size, never by guess.
tiers._warning: The :1.5b-base tag on this machine is NOT instruction-tuned and rambles. The instruct tag is the one to pull.

tiers.name: claude
tiers.costs: Claude Code subscription quota, NOT per-token API
tiers.note: Measured 3.6s round trip and correct, which is ~4x faster than the local 1.5b AND right. This is the primary path for anything needing judgement.
tiers._critical: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY must never be present in this subprocess's environment. With it set, every call becomes metered API spend instead of subscription quota — silently. The router strips it.

tiers.name: local-large
tiers.note: The floor. model:null means ask llm-recommend what this machine can actually hold, rather than hardcoding a tag that may not fit a different Mac.
tiers._why_last: Works with no network, no subscription and no key. Every demotion path ends here, so it must never itself depend on anything remote.

demotion._comment: What counts as 'this tier is unavailable'. Detected by FAILURE, never predicted — nothing in Claude Code exposes remaining quota, so guessing would mean demoting while the good path still worked.
demotion.note: A quota failure costs one slow request before the demotion. That is the honest price of having no quota signal to read.
